description: Is Trickster's caching working? Cache-engine outcomes per backend (hits, misses, origin status and latency), the object caches behind them (operations, hit ratio, latency, capacity, evictions, errors), and the static backend's in-memory Fileserver cache.

panels.title: Cache hit ratio
panels.description: Share of cache-engine executions over the dashboard range answered at least partly from cache: hit, phit (partial hit: the cached range served and only the missing part, usually the newest data, fetched), rhit (revalidated with the origin), nchit (negative cache) and proxy-hit (joined another request's in-flight fetch). Misses, purges, failures and native SQL statements that are never cached count against it. Only $backend traffic that ran through a caching engine (object cache, time series delta cache, native SQL) is counted; passthrough paths are not. Full hit ratio, next to it, leaves out phit.

targets.expr: (sum(increase(trickster_proxy_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", cache_status=~"hit|phit|rhit|nchit|proxy-hit"}[$__range])) or vector(0)) / (sum(increase(trickster_proxy_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend"}[$__range])) > 0) or vector(-1)

panels.title: Full hit ratio
panels.description: Share of cache-engine executions over the dashboard range served entirely from cache (hit, rhit, nchit, proxy-hit), leaving out partial hits. The gap to Cache hit ratio is the phit share: time series requests whose newest data came from the origin, which is the normal outcome for a refreshing dashboard on a delta-cached backend. That is why this tile has no good or bad color.

targets.expr: (sum(increase(trickster_proxy_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", cache_status=~"hit|rhit|nchit|proxy-hit"}[$__range])) or vector(0)) / (sum(increase(trickster_proxy_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend"}[$__range])) > 0) or vector(-1)

panels.title: Engine requests
panels.description: Cache-engine executions per second for $backend, all cache statuses. Not a client request count: internal partial-bucket fetches and Graphite multi-target renders add executions of their own, and passthrough (proxy handler, reverseproxy) traffic is absent. Use the HTTP Traffic dashboard for client requests.

targets.expr: sum(rate(trickster_proxy_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend"}[$__rate_interval])) or vector(0)

panels.title: Engine 5xx ratio
panels.description: Share of cache-engine executions for $backend that returned a 5xx status, over the last rate interval. Includes origin 5xx passed through or served from the negative cache, delta cache upstream failures (reported as 500 when the origin status was not an error) and native SQL proxy-error/error (a synthetic 500). Orange above 1%, red above 5%; the Errors by reason row names the backend.

targets.expr: (sum(rate(trickster_proxy_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", http_status=~"5.."}[$__rate_interval])) or vector(0)) / (sum(rate(trickster_proxy_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend"}[$__rate_interval])) > 0)

panels.title: Get hit ratio
panels.description: Share of object-cache lookups (operation get) over the dashboard range that found the key, for the caches in $cache. This is the storage layer, not the request layer: one client request can make several gets (delta cache, chunked caching, native SQL delta tiers), and every request waiting on a coalesced lookup is counted. Failed lookups are not gets; they appear as cache errors. Reads 'no lookups' when no selected cache was read in the range.

targets.expr: (sum(increase(trickster_cache_operation_objects_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", cache_name=~"$cache", operation="get", status="hit"}[$__range])) or vector(0)) / (sum(increase(trickster_cache_operation_objects_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", cache_name=~"$cache", operation="get"}[$__range])) > 0) or vector(-1)

panels.title: Cache errors/s
panels.description: Cache failures per second across $cache: lookups that failed with anything but key-not-found (a provider failure such as an unreachable or timing-out Redis/Valkey server) plus native SQL and TSM raw-cache object-tier failures. Oversized-entry refusals (reason *_max_object_size) are excluded as a size policy, not a fault. Requests still fall back to the origin. Failed stores on HTTP caches are not counted anywhere.

targets.expr: sum(rate(trickster_cache_events_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", cache_name=~"$cache", event="error", reason!~".*_max_object_size"}[$__rate_interval])) or vector(0)

panels.title: Size evictions
panels.description: Eviction passes over the dashboard range forced by capacity: size_bytes (over index.max_size_bytes), size_objects (over index.max_size_objects) or free_space (filesystem below min_free_bytes). Each pass removes a batch of up to 256 objects; TTL expiry passes are left out as normal churn. Only filesystem and bbolt caches report evictions, so the tile reads n/a when no selected cache is one of them: memory, redis, valkey and badger evict without reporting it. Frequent passes with no headroom mean the cache is undersized.

targets.expr: sum(increase(trickster_cache_events_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", cache_name=~"$cache", event="eviction", reason=~"size_bytes|size_objects|free_space"}[$__range])) or 0 * sum(trickster_cache_max_usage_bytes{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", cache_name=~"$cache"}) or vector(-1)

panels.title: Capacity used
panels.description: Highest used/configured ratio across $cache and instances, on bytes (index.max_size_bytes) or objects (index.max_size_objects, when not 0). Only filesystem and bbolt caches report capacity, so n/a means no selected cache is index-backed. A full disk cache settles just under 100%, since the reaper evicts to max minus the backoff; red above 105% means the reaper is not keeping up (or its worker died).

targets.expr: max(label_replace(trickster_cache_usage_bytes{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", cache_name=~"$cache"} / (trickster_cache_max_usage_bytes{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", cache_name=~"$cache"} > 0), "limit", "bytes", "", "") or label_replace(trickster_cache_usage_objects{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", cache_name=~"$cache"} / (trickster_cache_max_usage_objects{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", cache_name=~"$cache"} > 0), "limit", "objects", "", "")) or vector(-1)

panels.title: Engine requests/s by cache status
panels.description: Cache-engine executions per second for $backend, stacked by lookup status: hit (fully cached), phit (partly cached, the rest fetched; the normal case for refreshing time series dashboards), rhit (revalidated), nchit (negative cache), proxy-hit (joined an in-flight fetch), kmiss (not cached), rmiss (cached, but not the range asked for), purge (client asked for no-cache on a delta cache path), proxy-error/error (upstream or cache failure). proxy-only comes from native SQL statements that are never cached and from ALB merge members on uncached paths. The object cache skips client no-cache requests entirely, so purge only comes from the delta cache.

targets.expr: sum by (cache_status) (rate(trickster_proxy_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Cache hit ratio by backend
panels.description: Per backend, the share of cache-engine executions answered at least partly from cache (hit, phit, rhit, nchit, proxy-hit), over the rate interval: the same definition as the Cache hit ratio tile. A drop after a deploy or reload usually means a changed cache key or TTL, or an emptied cache. The table below splits out the full hit ratio; the Time Series Acceleration dashboard shows how many points were served from cache.

targets.expr: (sum by (backend_name) (rate(trickster_proxy_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", cache_status=~"hit|phit|rhit|nchit|proxy-hit"}[$__rate_interval])) or 0 * (sum by (backend_name) (rate(trickster_proxy_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend"}[$__rate_interval])) > 0)) / (sum by (backend_name) (rate(trickster_proxy_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend"}[$__rate_interval])) > 0)

panels.title: Engine responses/s by HTTP status
panels.description: Cache-engine executions per second for $backend by the exact HTTP status they returned, whether it came from the cache or the origin. Colors follow the status class (2xx green, 3xx blue, 4xx orange, 5xx red) with shades for common codes; 206 is a byte-range response. Native SQL listeners report a synthetic 200, or 500 for proxy-error/error.

targets.expr: sum by (http_status) (rate(trickster_proxy_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Mean engine latency by cache status
panels.description: Mean engine time per execution (_sum/_count) for $backend, by lookup status. A hit is cache read time; phit, kmiss, rmiss and purge include the origin fetch; proxy-hit reports the elapsed time of the shared fetch it joined. It excludes writing the response to the client, so it is not end-to-end latency. The histogram's smallest bucket is 50 ms, so means are used instead of quantiles. Object cache executions under 1 ms are not recorded at all, which biases hit means upward.

targets.expr: sum by (status) (rate(trickster_proxy_request_duration_seconds_sum{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend"}[$__rate_interval])) / (sum by (status) (rate(trickster_proxy_request_duration_seconds_count{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend"}[$__rate_interval])) > 0)

panels.title: Mean origin-fetch latency by backend
panels.description: Mean engine time of executions that went to the origin (status kmiss, rmiss, phit, purge), for the 10 slowest backends in $backend. This is the price of a miss; a rising line means the origin, or the path to it, is slowing down. Includes the cache write that follows the fetch, not the response write to the client.

targets.expr: topk(10, sum by (backend_name) (rate(trickster_proxy_request_duration_seconds_sum{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", status=~"kmiss|rmiss|phit|purge"}[$__rate_interval])) / (sum by (backend_name) (rate(trickster_proxy_request_duration_seconds_count{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", status=~"kmiss|rmiss|phit|purge"}[$__rate_interval])) > 0))

panels.title: Engine executions slower than 500 ms by backend
panels.description: Share of cache-engine executions taking longer than 500 ms, for the 10 worst backends in $backend, read from the 0.5 s histogram bucket (the buckets are 0.05, 0.1, 0.5, 1, 5, 10 and 20 s). The tail the mean hides: a backend with a fast mean and a high share here has a few very slow origin fetches. Object cache executions under 1 ms are not recorded, which slightly overstates the share.

targets.expr: topk(10, 1 - (sum by (backend_name) (rate(trickster_proxy_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", le="0.5"}[$__rate_interval])) / (sum by (backend_name) (rate(trickster_proxy_request_duration_seconds_count{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend"}[$__rate_interval])) > 0)))

panels.title: Cache status share (range)
panels.description: Cache-engine executions for $backend by lookup status over the dashboard's time range: the share served fully (hit), partly (phit), by revalidation (rhit) or from a joined fetch (proxy-hit), versus misses and errors. Status meanings are in Engine requests/s by cache status. Totals cover the dashboard's time range; hover a slice for its count.

targets.expr: sort_desc(sum by (cache_status) (increase(trickster_proxy_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend"}[$__range])) > 0)

panels.title: Engine status code share (range)
panels.description: Cache-engine executions for $backend by the exact HTTP status returned, from cache or origin, over the dashboard's time range. Native SQL listeners report a synthetic 200, or 500 for proxy-error/error. Totals cover the dashboard's time range; hover a slice for its count.

targets.expr: sort_desc(sum by (http_status) (increase(trickster_proxy_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend"}[$__range])) > 0)

panels.title: Cache engine summary by backend (range)
panels.description: One row per backend in $backend that ran cache-engine executions during the dashboard range: total executions, Cache hit ratio (hit, phit, rhit, nchit, proxy-hit), Full hit ratio (the same without phit), miss share (kmiss, rmiss, purge), 5xx share, mean engine latency and mean origin-fetch latency. Native SQL backends (MySQL, PostgreSQL wire, Flight SQL) appear under their engine name as provider; the SQL Wire Protocols dashboard breaks them down. ALB members are listed under their own names.

targets.expr: sum by (backend_name, provider) (increase(trickster_proxy_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend"}[$__range])) > 0

(sum by (backend_name, provider) (increase(trickster_proxy_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", cache_status=~"hit|phit|rhit|nchit|proxy-hit"}[$__range])) or 0 * (sum by (backend_name, provider) (increase(trickster_proxy_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend"}[$__range])) > 0)) / (sum by (backend_name, provider) (increase(trickster_proxy_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend"}[$__range])) > 0)

(sum by (backend_name, provider) (increase(trickster_proxy_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", cache_status=~"hit|rhit|nchit|proxy-hit"}[$__range])) or 0 * (sum by (backend_name, provider) (increase(trickster_proxy_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend"}[$__range])) > 0)) / (sum by (backend_name, provider) (increase(trickster_proxy_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend"}[$__range])) > 0)

(sum by (backend_name, provider) (increase(trickster_proxy_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", cache_status=~"kmiss|rmiss|purge"}[$__range])) or 0 * (sum by (backend_name, provider) (increase(trickster_proxy_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend"}[$__range])) > 0)) / (sum by (backend_name, provider) (increase(trickster_proxy_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend"}[$__range])) > 0)

(sum by (backend_name, provider) (increase(trickster_proxy_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", http_status=~"5.."}[$__range])) or 0 * (sum by (backend_name, provider) (increase(trickster_proxy_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend"}[$__range])) > 0)) / (sum by (backend_name, provider) (increase(trickster_proxy_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend"}[$__range])) > 0)

sum by (backend_name, provider) (rate(trickster_proxy_request_duration_seconds_sum{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend"}[$__range])) / (sum by (backend_name, provider) (rate(trickster_proxy_request_duration_seconds_count{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend"}[$__range])) > 0)

sum by (backend_name, provider) (rate(trickster_proxy_request_duration_seconds_sum{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", status=~"kmiss|rmiss|phit|purge"}[$__range])) / (sum by (backend_name, provider) (rate(trickster_proxy_request_duration_seconds_count{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", status=~"kmiss|rmiss|phit|purge"}[$__range])) > 0)

panels.title: Cache operations/s by operation and status
panels.description: Object-cache operations per second across $cache. get is split into hit and kmiss; set is a store, setDirect a store by reference (memory provider only), del a removal call or a reaper eviction batch (filesystem and bbolt). A set is counted even when the provider failed to store it. Every request waiting on a coalesced lookup counts its own get.

targets.expr: sum by (status) (rate(trickster_cache_operation_objects_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", cache_name=~"$cache", operation="get"}[$__rate_interval]))
sum by (operation) (rate(trickster_cache_operation_objects_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", cache_name=~"$cache", operation!="get"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Get hit ratio by cache
panels.description: Per cache, the share of get operations that found the key, over the rate interval. It is a storage-layer ratio and differs from the engines' Cache hit ratio: delta and chunked caches make several gets per request, and a phit is a get hit followed by an origin fetch. Failed lookups are not gets, so during a cache-server outage the line thins out or breaks while cache errors rise, rather than dropping to 0.

targets.expr: (sum by (cache_name) (rate(trickster_cache_operation_objects_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", cache_name=~"$cache", operation="get", status="hit"}[$__rate_interval])) or 0 * (sum by (cache_name) (rate(trickster_cache_operation_objects_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", cache_name=~"$cache", operation="get"}[$__rate_interval])) > 0)) / (sum by (cache_name) (rate(trickster_cache_operation_objects_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", cache_name=~"$cache", operation="get"}[$__rate_interval])) > 0)

panels.title: Cache throughput by operation
panels.description: Payload bytes per second across $cache: get is bytes read on hits (for a large object streamed from disk, its full size at open), set the bytes stored, setDirect the estimated in-memory size of objects stored by reference, and del the bytes freed by removals and evictions (filesystem and bbolt only).

targets.expr: sum by (operation) (rate(trickster_cache_operation_bytes_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", cache_name=~"$cache"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Average object size by cache
panels.description: Mean payload size per cache: read is bytes per get hit, write is bytes per set or setDirect. Growth in read size raises cache latency and memory per request; compare with the backend's max_object_size_bytes. setDirect sizes are estimates. Removal sizes are not shown because a del counts calls and batches, not keys.

targets.expr: sum by (cache_name) (rate(trickster_cache_operation_bytes_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", cache_name=~"$cache", operation="get", status="hit"}[$__rate_interval])) / (sum by (cache_name) (rate(trickster_cache_operation_objects_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", cache_name=~"$cache", operation="get", status="hit"}[$__rate_interval])) > 0)

sum by (cache_name) (rate(trickster_cache_operation_bytes_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", cache_name=~"$cache", operation=~"set|setDirect"}[$__rate_interval])) / (sum by (cache_name) (rate(trickster_cache_operation_objects_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", cache_name=~"$cache", operation=~"set|setDirect"}[$__rate_interval])) > 0)

panels.title: Mean cache operation latency
panels.description: Mean wall time per operation (_sum/_count) by cache and operation. A get includes any wait on a coalesced lookup; a del by the reaper times a whole eviction batch. Memory should be microseconds, Redis/Valkey about one network round trip, filesystem and bbolt depend on the disk. The histogram's smallest bucket is 50 ms, so quantiles would be interpolation; means are used instead.

targets.expr: sum by (cache_name, operation) (rate(trickster_cache_operation_duration_seconds_sum{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", cache_name=~"$cache"}[$__rate_interval])) / (sum by (cache_name, operation) (rate(trickster_cache_operation_duration_seconds_count{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", cache_name=~"$cache"}[$__rate_interval])) > 0)

panels.title: Cache operations slower than 50 ms
panels.description: Share of operations by cache and operation that took longer than 50 ms (the histogram's smallest bucket). For a cache this is the tail signal: it should be near 0 for memory and Redis/Valkey. A rising share means a slow disk, a saturated or distant cache server, or contention.

targets.expr: 1 - (sum by (cache_name, operation) (rate(trickster_cache_operation_duration_seconds_bucket{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", cache_name=~"$cache", le="0.05"}[$__rate_interval])) / (sum by (cache_name, operation) (rate(trickster_cache_operation_duration_seconds_count{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", cache_name=~"$cache"}[$__rate_interval])) > 0))

panels.title: Cache summary (range)
panels.description: One row per cache in $cache over the dashboard range: cache provider, average operations/s, get hit ratio, average read and write bytes/s, mean get latency, share of operations over 50 ms, and failures (event error, without refusals to store oversized entries, which are a size policy rather than a fault). The provider column names the cache provider (memory, filesystem, bbolt, badger, redis, valkey), not the backend provider. A cache that is configured but unused has no row.

targets.expr: sum by (cache_name, provider) (rate(trickster_cache_operation_objects_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", cache_name=~"$cache"}[$__range]))

(sum by (cache_name, provider) (increase(trickster_cache_operation_objects_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", cache_name=~"$cache", operation="get", status="hit"}[$__range])) or 0 * (sum by (cache_name, provider) (increase(trickster_cache_operation_objects_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", cache_name=~"$cache", operation="get"}[$__range])) > 0)) / (sum by (cache_name, provider) (increase(trickster_cache_operation_objects_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", cache_name=~"$cache", operation="get"}[$__range])) > 0)
sum by (cache_name, provider) (rate(trickster_cache_operation_bytes_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", cache_name=~"$cache", operation="get"}[$__range]))
sum by (cache_name, provider) (rate(trickster_cache_operation_bytes_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", cache_name=~"$cache", operation=~"set|setDirect"}[$__range]))

sum by (cache_name, provider) (rate(trickster_cache_operation_duration_seconds_sum{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", cache_name=~"$cache", operation="get"}[$__range])) / (sum by (cache_name, provider) (rate(trickster_cache_operation_duration_seconds_count{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", cache_name=~"$cache", operation="get"}[$__range])) > 0)

1 - (sum by (cache_name, provider) (rate(trickster_cache_operation_duration_seconds_bucket{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", cache_name=~"$cache", le="0.05"}[$__range])) / (sum by (cache_name, provider) (rate(trickster_cache_operation_duration_seconds_count{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", cache_name=~"$cache"}[$__range])) > 0))

sum by (cache_name, provider) (increase(trickster_cache_events_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", cache_name=~"$cache", event="error", reason!~".*_max_object_size"}[$__range])) or 0 * sum by (cache_name, provider) (rate(trickster_cache_operation_objects_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", cache_name=~"$cache"}[$__range]))

panels.title: Cache bytes used vs max
panels.description: Bytes tracked by the Cache Index (sum of stored payload sizes) against index.max_size_bytes (dashed), per cache, on the fullest instance. Filesystem and bbolt caches only: memory, redis, valkey and badger export no capacity. On-disk use is larger (headers, keys, journal, block overhead). After a reload that rebuilds a filesystem cache, usage can read 0 until the next write.

targets.expr: max by (cache_name) (trickster_cache_usage_bytes{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", cache_name=~"$cache"})
max by (cache_name) (trickster_cache_max_usage_bytes{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", cache_name=~"$cache"})

panels.title: Cache objects vs max
panels.description: Objects tracked by the Cache Index against index.max_size_objects (dashed), per cache, on the fullest instance. The object limit defaults to 0 (no limit) and is drawn only when set. Filesystem and bbolt caches only. A removed or renamed cache leaves a flat 0 series until restart.

targets.expr: max by (cache_name) (trickster_cache_usage_objects{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", cache_name=~"$cache"})
max by (cache_name) (trickster_cache_max_usage_objects{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", cache_name=~"$cache"} > 0)

panels.title: Eviction passes/s by reason
panels.description: Reaper eviction passes per second by cache and reason. Each pass removes a batch of up to 256 objects; the number of objects evicted is not exported. ttl is expired objects being cleaned up (normal); size_bytes and size_objects mean the cache hit its configured limit and evicted the least recently used down to max minus the backoff; free_space means the filesystem fell below min_free_bytes. Emitted by filesystem and bbolt caches only; memory (ristretto), redis, valkey and badger evict without telling Trickster.

targets.expr: sum by (cache_name, reason) (rate(trickster_cache_events_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", cache_name=~"$cache", event="eviction"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Capacity utilization
panels.description: Used/configured ratio per filesystem or bbolt cache, for bytes and (when index.max_size_objects is set) objects, on the fullest instance. A full cache holds just under 100%; above 105% the reaper is not keeping up. Caches of other providers do not appear.

targets.expr: max by (cache_name) (trickster_cache_usage_bytes{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", cache_name=~"$cache"} / (trickster_cache_max_usage_bytes{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", cache_name=~"$cache"} > 0))

max by (cache_name) (trickster_cache_usage_objects{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", cache_name=~"$cache"} / (trickster_cache_max_usage_objects{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", cache_name=~"$cache"} > 0))

panels.title: Cache errors/s by reason
panels.description: Cache failures per second by cache and reason, top 10. 'failed to retrieve cache entry' is a lookup that failed with something other than key-not-found (server unreachable, timeout, provider read failure), counted once per waiting request. <protocol>_<failure> reasons (mysql, pgwire, flightsql, tsm_global_raw) come from native SQL and TSM raw-series caches; *_max_object_size is a refusal to store an oversized entry, not a fault. None of these fail the client request: a failed lookup goes to the origin and a failed store is simply not cached.

targets.expr: topk(10, sum by (cache_name, reason) (rate(trickster_cache_events_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", cache_name=~"$cache", event="error"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: Engine errors/s by backend
panels.description: Cache-engine executions per second for $backend that failed (cache_status proxy-error or error) or returned a 5xx, by backend, status and code, top 10. proxy-error is an upstream failure (an origin error, or a delta cache fetch that could not complete), also given to every request that was waiting on that fetch; error is a cache lookup or handling failure. A 5xx with a hit or nchit status is an error served from cache.

targets.expr: topk(10, sum by (backend_name, cache_status, http_status) (rate(trickster_proxy_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", cache_status=~"proxy-error|error"}[$__rate_interval]) or rate(trickster_proxy_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$backend", http_status=~"5.."}[$__rate_interval]))) > 0

panels.title: Cache errors by reason (range)
panels.description: Cache failures over the dashboard range by cache, cache provider and reason, largest first; only reasons that occurred are listed. Use it to tell a cache-server outage (failed to retrieve cache entry on a redis or valkey cache) from native SQL object-tier problems (decode_failure, store_failure) and size refusals (max_object_size).

targets.expr: sort_desc(sum by (cache_name, provider, reason) (increase(trickster_cache_events_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", cache_name=~"$cache", event="error"}[$__range])) > 0)

panels.title: Unservable objects removed by reason
panels.description: Objects found unservable on read or during a sweep and removed, per second, by cache and reason. expired is normal churn; unknown_format follows an upgrade that changed the stored format (the cache refills); corrupt means damaged data on disk and should be 0. Objects of 10 MiB or more are checked after being served, so a corrupt one is served once. Filesystem and bbolt caches only.

targets.expr: sum by (cache_name, reason) (rate(trickster_cache_events_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", cache_name=~"$cache", event="invalid_object"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Index maintenance (range)
panels.description: Per filesystem or bbolt cache over the dashboard range: index journal compactions, completed sweeps, objects a sweep adopted (on disk but missing from the index, e.g. after an unclean shutdown) or dropped (in the index but gone from disk), and corrupt objects removed. Sweeps run every index.scan_interval (24h by default) and at startup when the persisted index can't be trusted; compactions run when the journal reaches half the snapshot size.

targets.expr: sum by (cache_name) (increase(trickster_cache_events_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", cache_name=~"$cache", event="index", reason="compaction"}[$__range]))
sum by (cache_name) (increase(trickster_cache_events_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", cache_name=~"$cache", event="index", reason="sweep"}[$__range]))
sum by (cache_name) (increase(trickster_cache_events_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", cache_name=~"$cache", event="sweep", reason="adopted"}[$__range]))
sum by (cache_name) (increase(trickster_cache_events_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", cache_name=~"$cache", event="sweep", reason="dropped"}[$__range]))

sum by (cache_name) (increase(trickster_cache_events_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", cache_name=~"$cache", event="invalid_object", reason="corrupt"}[$__range])) or 0 * sum by (cache_name) (increase(trickster_cache_events_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", cache_name=~"$cache", event="index"}[$__range]))

panels.title: Index panics
panels.description: Recovered panics in a Cache Index worker (flusher, reaper or scanner) over the dashboard range, across all caches of the selected instances (the metric has no cache name; the log does). A panicked worker stays stopped until a reload or restart rebuilds the cache: without the reaper a disk cache grows past its limits, without the flusher the persisted index goes stale. Any value is critical.

targets.expr: sum(increase(trickster_cache_index_panic_recovered_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[$__range])) or vector(0)

panels.title: Client-side cache hits/s by cache
panels.description: Valkey reads answered from the in-process client-side cache instead of the server, per second. Present only for provider valkey caches with valkey.client_side_cache.enabled: true (the series starts at 0 on connect); empty otherwise. These hits are a subset of the cache's get hits, and an entry lives at most client_side_cache.max_ttl.

targets.expr: sum by (cache_name) (rate(trickster_cache_events_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", cache_name=~"$cache", event="client_cache_hit"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Share of get hits served client-side
panels.description: Per Valkey cache with the client-side cache enabled, the share of get hits answered locally without a server round trip. Higher means less network latency and server load; a low share with many hits suggests a short max_ttl, a small size_bytes_per_connection, or keys changing often (each change invalidates every instance's copy).

targets.expr: sum by (cache_name) (rate(trickster_cache_events_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", cache_name=~"$cache", event="client_cache_hit"}[$__rate_interval])) / (sum by (cache_name) (rate(trickster_cache_operation_objects_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", cache_name=~"$cache", operation="get", status="hit"}[$__rate_interval])) > 0)

panels.title: Files served/s by cache status
panels.description: Files sent per second by provider static backends in $static, by Fileserver cache status: hit (held in memory, sent as held), phit (held file compressed for this response, the rendition then held), kmiss (read from disk, then held) and disk (sent from disk without being held: Range requests, HEAD or 304 answers, files over static.cache.max_file_size_bytes, or the cache disabled). Responses with no file (404s without not_found_file, redirects, listings) are not counted.

targets.expr: sum by (cache_status) (rate(trickster_fileserver_responses_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$static"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Fileserver memory hit ratio
panels.description: Per static backend, the share of files served from memory (hit or phit). A falling ratio with evictions in the panel below means static.cache.max_size_bytes or max_files is too small for the working set; a ratio of 0 with disk responses only means the cache is disabled or the files are too large to hold.

targets.expr: (sum by (backend_name) (rate(trickster_fileserver_responses_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$static", cache_status=~"hit|phit"}[$__rate_interval])) or 0 * (sum by (backend_name) (rate(trickster_fileserver_responses_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$static"}[$__rate_interval])) > 0)) / (sum by (backend_name) (rate(trickster_fileserver_responses_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$static"}[$__rate_interval])) > 0)

panels.title: Encodings served (range)
panels.description: Files sent by content encoding over the dashboard range, across $static. identity is the file as stored; zstd, br, gzip and deflate are held or on-the-fly compressed renditions chosen from the client's Accept-Encoding. Files under 512 bytes are always sent as identity.

targets.expr: sum by (encoding) (increase(trickster_fileserver_responses_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$static"}[$__range])) > 0

panels.title: Fileserver cache bytes vs max
panels.description: Accounted bytes held by each static backend's Fileserver cache against static.cache.max_size_bytes (dashed). Each object counts its size plus its key and a fixed 1 KiB, so many tiny files reach the limit long before their bodies would; loads in progress are reserved up front. This is the static backend's own in-memory cache, separate from the caches above, and is present while static.cache is enabled (the default).

targets.expr: max by (backend_name) (trickster_fileserver_cache_usage_bytes{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$static"})
max by (backend_name) (trickster_fileserver_cache_max_usage_bytes{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$static"})

panels.title: Fileserver cache objects vs max_files
panels.description: Objects held by each static backend's Fileserver cache against static.cache.max_files (dashed). Every rendition is its own object, so one file held as identity, gzip and br counts 3; loads in progress count too.

targets.expr: max by (backend_name) (trickster_fileserver_cache_usage_objects{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$static"})
max by (backend_name) (trickster_fileserver_cache_max_usage_objects{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$static"})

panels.title: Fileserver evictions and invalidations
panels.description: Objects removed from each Fileserver cache per second. eviction: dropped to make room (sustained evictions mean max_size_bytes or max_files is too small). invalidation: dropped because the file changed on disk, revalidation found it stale, or the cache was purged. A config reload that replaces a static backend purges its old cache and counts every held object as an invalidation, so expect a spike at each reload annotation; don't alert on it.

targets.expr: sum by (backend_name, event) (rate(trickster_fileserver_cache_events_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", backend_name=~"$static"}[$__rate_interval]))

list.name: datasource

list.description: The Prometheus-compatible data source that scrapes Trickster's /metrics endpoint.

list.label: Job
list.description: Scrape job(s) holding the Trickster targets.

list.name: backend
list.label: Backend
list.description: Backends whose requests run through a caching engine (object cache, time series delta cache or a native SQL listener). Passthrough-only backends never appear. Filters the engine panels.

list.name: cache
list.label: Cache
list.description: Configured caches (caches.<name>) that have served at least one operation. Filters the object cache, capacity, error, index and Valkey panels.

list.label: Static backend
list.description: Provider static backends. Filters the Static file server row.
